record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Is the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation itself in the KPZ universality class, in the sense that one can rigorously prove the characteristic 3:2:1 scaling between time, spatial correlations, and fluctuations for its solutions?

evidence.quote: A basic question is whether KPZ is in the KPZ universality class. In other words, can one show rigorously that solutions of KPZ indeed have the KPZ scaling 3 : 2 : 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) stochastic partial differential equation
$$\partial_t h(t,x) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,\partial_x^2 h(t,x) \;+\; \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\partial_x h(t,x)\bigr)^2 \;+\; \xi(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb{R},$$
where $\xi$ is space–time white noise on $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\times\mathbb{R}$, and $h$ is interpreted via the Cole–Hopf transformation $h(t,x) = \log Z(t,x)$, with $Z$ the solution of the multiplicative stochastic heat equation $\partial_t Z = \tfrac{1}{2}\partial_x^2 Z + Z\,\xi$.

The KPZ universality class is characterized by the 1:2:3 scaling (equivalently written 3:2:1): fluctuations of the height grow like $t^{1/3}$, non-trivial spatial correlations occur on scales of order $t^{2/3}$, and these are coupled through the time scale $t$. Concretely, for a suitable centering constant $C$, define the rescaled height
$$h_\varepsilon(t,x) \;=\; \varepsilon^{1/2}\Bigl(h\bigl(\varepsilon^{-3/2}t,\ \varepsilon^{-1}x\bigr) + C\,\varepsilon^{-3/2}t\Bigr).$$

Prove rigorously that, starting from a suitable class of initial data, the random fields $h_\varepsilon$ converge as $\varepsilon\to 0$ to a non-degenerate scale-invariant limit (the KPZ fixed point), thereby establishing that the KPZ equation itself lies in the KPZ universality class with the characteristic 1:2:3 scaling exponents between fluctuations, spatial correlations, and time.
artifact.status_search_result: Quastel and Sarkar (arXiv:2008.06584, published in J. Amer. Math. Soc.) proved that under the 1:2:3 scaling the KPZ equation converges to the KPZ fixed point for a broad class of initial data, establishing rigorously that the KPZ equation belongs to the KPZ universality class with the characteristic scaling exponents. Subsequent works (Virág; Wu) have extended and strengthened this result.

status_evidence.title: Convergence of exclusion processes and the KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point
status_evidence.snippet: Under the 1:2:3 scaling... the height function of... the KPZ equation converge to the KPZ fixed point.
status_evidence.claim: The KPZ equation, under 1:2:3 scaling, converges to the KPZ fixed point, confirming it lies in the KPZ universality class.

status_evidence.title: KPZ fixed point - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The KPZ fixed point is a Markov process that is conjectured to be the universal limit of all models in the KPZ universality class.
status_evidence.claim: The KPZ fixed point is the universal scale-invariant limit, and convergence of the KPZ equation to it has been established.
